Viewed through standard monetary economics, this is a “dovish hike.” With sticky prices à la Calvo (1983), keeping the policy rate below its longer-run neutral supports output while inflation closes in on target. The Committee’s “symmetric” 2 percent goal and persistently low market-based inflation compensation point to anchored or even modestly low expected inflation, aligning with the expectations-augmented Phillips curve insights of Friedman and Phelps (no long-run unemployment–inflation trade-off) and with interest-rate rule frameworks such as McCallum and Nelson (1999), which favor measured adjustments when inflation expectations are well anchored. The emphasis on gradualism under uncertainty echoes Brainard-style caution, and continued balance-sheet reinvestment helps keep term premiums and financial conditions accommodative. Net effect: rate increase acknowledged, but guidance and reinvestment tilt supportive for growth and risk assets, so sentiment is mildly positive.
